transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lina Park (CSM), Priya Kapoor (Suncrest Head of Data), Marcus Lee (Platform), Olivia Barnes (CPO), Ethan Cole (ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya with Redwood — excited to kick off Suncrest's onboarding. quick round robin real quick, i think we have about 45 minutes.
[00:18] Priya Kapoor: thanks Maya, Priya here. happy to be on, want to make sure we cover security and timelines — we've got a Q4 internal launch target.
[00:30] Daniel Ortiz: hi all, i'm Daniel on the SE side, i'll own the technical intake and the private deployment deep dive.
[00:40] Marcus Lee: Marcus here, platform eng, i'll be the main infra contact. we run k8s on aws, vpc to vpc peering is doable.
[00:50] Olivia Barnes: Olivia, chief privacy, i need to understand data residency and what logs you retain. SOC two compliance is a must.
[01:05] Maya Chen: perfect, quick agenda: run through milestones, clarify deployment mode options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security checklist, and then action items and next steps.
[01:22] Ethan Cole: real quick, are we expecting to use Redwood's embedding endpoint for semantic search or full generation? if both, we need to discuss cost implications.
[01:34] Lina Park: we'll note that — most customers do embeddings + generation; Redwood has recommendations for batching and cache to control cost.
[01:45] Priya Kapoor: timeline: we want an internal beta by mid-november. is that realistic if we do private deployment?
[01:58] Daniel Ortiz: it's tight but possible. private deployment adds lead time — network setup and certificate exchange usually 2–3 weeks. Dedicated reserved pools are faster but require commit. hosted is fastest to prod, but restricted for some regulated data.
[02:15] Marcus Lee: for Suncrest some PHI goes through the pipeline; we likely need VPC/private where traffic never leaves our account.
[02:25] Olivia Barnes: correct — we need an architecture where logs and prompt content can be kept in our S3 and keys in our KMS/HSM.
[02:38] Daniel Ortiz: Redwood's private package supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem key material; there's an audit log option. we'll share the security pack. note: sometimes the transcript says "Redwood Influence" — that's just the service name, sorry, but it's Redwood Inference.
[02:56] Maya Chen: okay security items: SOC2 report, encryption at rest, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. Olivia, do you have any additional must-haves?
[03:10] Olivia Barnes: data residency — events must be kept in the US east region, and retention default of 30 days but configurable. also we need ptr for any subpoena or audit trail.
[03:26] Daniel Ortiz: noted. we'll produce a runbook that maps where logs live, retention controls, and how to configure KMS/HSM integration.
[03:36] Priya Kapoor: on performance — we need sub-200ms p99 for short completions (~128 tokens) for our triage UI. is that realistic?
[03:48] Daniel Ortiz: with dedicated capacity and optimized kernels we can hit that depending on model and quantization. if you want fallbacks, we can route to smaller model variants when capacity is constrained. 
[04:02] Marcus Lee: what about batching? our traffic is spiky; we want good latency during spikes.
[04:12] Lina Park: Redwood supports continuous batching, and we can set latency SLOs. CS will propose autoscaling and burst policy recommendations for your workload.
[04:24] Ethan Cole: do you have guidance on prompt caching? we have many redundant prefixes across users.
[04:34] Daniel Ortiz: yes, prefix/KV cache can be enabled to reduce token costs and improve latency for repeated prompts — we'll include config examples.
[04:45] Maya Chen: let's talk integrations: Marcus, how do you want to handle the network handoff — VPC peering or private link?
[04:56] Marcus Lee: we prefer VPC peering to route directly, but PrivateLink might be better for security; we need the network diagrams to review.
[05:07] Daniel Ortiz: we'll produce both patterns in the runbook, including sample route tables and security group entries.
[05:18] Priya Kapoor: onboarding tasks — who will manage the pilot evaluation and metrics?
[05:26] Lina Park: CSM (me) will coordinate, but we'll lean on Ethan and Priya for prompt sets and sign-off criteria. typically we track latency, token cost per request, and quality regressions against your prompt eval set.
[05:40] Ethan Cole: on quality, we'll provide 200 canonical prompts and expected outputs; can Redwood run regression alerts?
[05:50] Daniel Ortiz: yes, Redwood Optimize can run periodic evals and alert on regressions; we'll need you to label tolerance thresholds.
[06:02] Olivia Barnes: legal note — we need a data processing addendum and clarity on retention of logs for audit.
[06:12] Maya Chen: legal and procurement will follow up; i'll attach our standard DPA and SLA.
[06:20] Priya Kapoor: any blockers you foresee?
[06:25] Daniel Ortiz: only lead time for private deployment and getting KMS access if you use HSM. we should schedule the deep dive early so infra can prep.
[06:35] Marcus Lee: timeline constraints — mid-nov beta. if deep dive is next week that helps.
[06:43] Maya Chen: proposed dates: next thursday (2026-10-08) for the 90-minute deep dive?
[06:52] Priya Kapoor: that works for us.
[06:55] Maya Chen: excellent. i'll send an invite.
[07:00] Daniel Ortiz: technical checklist highlights i'll deliver: network ports, tls cert exchange, KMS integration, model pinning and rate limits, backlog for canary rollouts.
[07:12] Ethan Cole: about model pinning — we need deterministic behavior across versions for auditability; can we pin model hashes?
[07:22] Daniel Ortiz: yes, Redwood supports exact model version pinning and rollouts with automatic fallback policies if there's a performance regression.
[07:33] Priya Kapoor: pricing — can you outline committed dedicated capacity vs pay-as-you-go hosted so we can size budget?
[07:44] Maya Chen: i'll send a pricing sheet with committed tiers and burst pricing. committed nodes reduce unit cost but require a monthly/annual commit. we can also propose a small pilot on hosted while private is being provisioned.
[07:58] Olivia Barnes: please include encryption-in-transit and at-rest details in the security packet.
[08:05] Daniel Ortiz: will do; also i'll include a checkbox for KMS vs HSM workflows.
[08:12] Priya Kapoor: for the pilot eval, expected success criteria: p99 latency <200ms for 128 tokens, embedding retrieval accuracy >85% on our eval set, and cost per active session under threshold X (we'll define X).
[08:30] Lina Park: we'll capture that in the project plan.
[08:38] Maya Chen: quick recap and owners: Redwood shares runbook, security pack, and pricing. SE schedules deep dive on 2026-10-08. Suncrest provides prompt set and retention rules. CSM adds milestones to activation tracker.
[08:55] Priya Kapoor: yep, and legal will review DPA once you send it.
[09:02] Maya Chen: any final questions?
[09:05] Marcus Lee: none from infra.
[09:08] Olivia Barnes: none. thanks everyone.
[09:12] Maya Chen: thanks team, we'll follow up with notes and the invite.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "Redwood Influence" mislabel). Speaker turns sometimes overlap.
